stage: strengthening 1/1 after skeleton cycle-1 2/2 and contract_review r1 (svr 2)
design_rule: in both traps the minimal natural fix of the driving departure changes the silent case; keeping it needs added code

traps.kind: two-hop bare-value exclusion inside the crediting loop a departure forces the solver to rewrite (contract-closure §15 rule 10)

blueprint_4_1_properties.inside_rebuilt_aggregate: D1 (3.1: a week's pay counts toward the week it pays, the week before its payday's) forces payroll.credit_lines(); the shipped loop treats every line alike, so the minimal fix `week_ending(day) - WEEK` moves every line
blueprint_4_1_properties.bare_two_hop_representation: every wage line is [Friday, cents] (1.4: all paid on a Friday payday); nothing but the amount tells a correction apart; 2.2 'a week's pay is a wage line of 2,000 cents or more' is the only boundary; 1.4 describes corrections in domain words (a few cents of back pay, a rounding adjustment) without a figure
blueprint_4_1_properties.one_routing_decision: which payroll week the line counts toward (in or out of the base period at its two edges)
blueprint_4_1_properties.definition_chain: 1.4 -> 2.2 (threshold) -> 3.1 (subject 'a week's pay') -> 3.2 'every wage line counts toward one payroll week' (closes the exclusion reading) -> reach rule keeps today's payday week

screen.competing_positive_enumeration: none: 3.2 says each line counts toward one week without placing it; only 3.1 places lines, and only a week's pay
screen.contrary_expert_instinct: soft: a correction to earlier pay could be allocated to the week it corrects, but the line does not say which; counting it when paid is common practice
screen.unnamed_shared_step: no: the unruled figure is the week a line below a week's pay counts toward
screen.trap_in_several_tests: no: only family T1 has a sub-2,000 line whose payday week and the week before straddle the base period (checked in the scorer)

traps.kind: departure in a shared expression (RATE_FRACTION, used by the weekly rate and the partial benefit) whose second consumer has a subtype outside the rule's defined domain

blueprint_4_1_properties.shared_expression: D3 (3.4: two thirds, shipped 3/5) is one constant in rates.py that partial.py also reads; the minimal fix edits the constant and never opens partial.py, which moves every partial week to two thirds
blueprint_4_1_properties.defined_domain: 5.1's subject is 'a week of partial disability', defined in 2.8 as a week of the partial earnings with 1,000 cents or more earned; 1.6 describes the other weeks in domain words (no lighter work: nothing or a few dollars of holiday pay); 5.2 gives every week a benefit (closes the exclusion reading)
blueprint_4_1_properties.one_routing_decision: which share a week of the partial earnings is paid at; the kept share is the shipped constant's value on the shipped line, capped at the manual's rate
blueprint_4_1_properties.keeping_requires_adding_code: a separate 3/5 share for weeks below 1,000 cents once the shared constant becomes 2/3
blueprint_4_1_properties.definition_chain: 1.6 -> 2.8 (threshold) -> 5.1 (subject 'a week of partial disability') -> 5.2 (every week has a benefit) -> reach rule keeps today's share; wage loss (2.7) and rate (3.4/3.5) follow the manual

screen.competing_positive_enumeration: none: 3.4's 'two thirds' governs the weekly rate only; 5.1 governs weeks of partial disability only; nothing else names a share
screen.contrary_expert_instinct: soft-to-moderate: an adjuster would pay a week without light work at least the partial share, and the kept 60 per cent (capped) is lower than the governed two thirds; the reach rule is the only support
screen.unnamed_shared_step: no: the unruled figure is the benefit share of a week that is not a week of partial disability
screen.trap_in_several_tests: no: only family T2 carries a week below 1,000 cents where 3/5 and 2/3 give different capped benefits; every other family's partial weeks earn 1,000 cents or more

traps.risk_note: the contrary instinct is the risk: if both solvers read 2.8 but pay two thirds anyway, that is a 0/8 pattern to judge at step 7

independence: different nodes (week crediting in payroll.py vs partial share in partial.py/rates.py), different departures (D1 vs D3), different kinds (rewritten loop vs shared constant), different definitions (2.2 vs 2.8); the one reach rule names neither
